Let $F$ be force, $m$ mass, and $a$ acceleration. \[\text{F=m a}\]
Let $p$ be momentum. Let $m$ be mass. Let $v$ be velocity. Linear momentum is defined by $p=m v$.
Let $K$ be energy. Let $m$ be mass. Let $v$ be velocity. The kinetic energy is \[K=\frac{1}{2}m v^2\].
Let $U$ be energy. Let $m$ be mass. Let $g$ be acceleration. Let $h$ be a length. Near a uniform gravitational field, use $U=m g h$.
Let $F$ be force. Let $k$ be stiffness. Let $x$ be a length. A linear spring obeys \[F=-k x\].
Let $F$ be force. Let $c$ be a damping coefficient. Let $v$ be velocity. A viscous damper is modeled by $F_d=-c v$.
Mechanical work along a path is \[W=\int_C \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{r}.\]
Let $P$ be power. Let $F$ be force. Let $v$ be velocity. Instantaneous mechanical power is $P=\mathbf{F}\cdot\mathbf{v}$.
Impulse over the interval is \[J=\int_{t_0}^{t_1}F(t)\,dt.\]
Torque about the origin is $\boldsymbol{\tau}=\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{F}$.
Angular momentum is \[\mathbf{L}=\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{p}.\]
For a fixed axis, the rotational equation is $\tau=I\alpha$.
Newtonian attraction has magnitude \[F=G\frac{m_1m_2}{r^2}.\]
Let $a$ be acceleration. Let $v$ be velocity. Let $r$ be a length. Uniform circular motion has acceleration $a_c=v^2/r$.
The undamped oscillator satisfies \[m\ddot{x}+kx=0.\]
The damped oscillator equation is $m\ddot{x}+c\dot{x}+kx=0$.
Define the mechanical Lagrangian by \[L=T-U.\]
A generalized coordinate obeys $\frac{d}{dt}\frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot q}-\frac{\partial L}{\partial q}=0$.
Hamilton's equation includes \[\dot q_i=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}.\]
Mass conservation in a continuum is $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf{v})=0$.
A local momentum balance is \[\rho\mathbf{a}=\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}+\rho\mathbf{b}.\]
